steps.en: What you see: Colour shows a systolic jet from ventricle to atrium, often posteriorly directed when the anterior leaflet prolapses or flails. The left atrium and left ventricle dilate in chronic severe disease. The continuous wave envelope is dense and the pulmonary vein shows systolic flow reversal when regurgitation is severe. Rheumatic disease with restricted leaflets is a common cause in Indian practice alongside prolapse and ischaemic tethering.

Normal values with units: Effective regurgitant orifice by PISA. Mild below 0.20 sq cm. Moderate 0.20 to 0.39 sq cm. Severe 0.40 sq cm or more.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on mitral regurgitation quantitation
Regurgitant volume. Mild below 30 ml. Moderate 30 to 59 ml. Severe 60 ml or more per beat.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on mitral regurgitation quantitation
Vena contracta width. Mild below 3 mm. Severe 7 mm or more measured at the narrowest neck.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on vena contracta

Left ventricular end systolic diameter. Surgery is considered at 40 mm or more in severe primary disease even without symptoms.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular size

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Left atrial enlargement gives broad P waves in lead two. Atrial fibrillation follows in chronic severe disease. Left ventricular hypertrophy shows a volume pattern with tall R waves.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A pansystolic murmur at the apex radiates to the axilla. The first sound softens and the second sound splits widely. A third sound marks the volume loaded ventricle.

spot.en: Landmarks: Mitral leaflet tips and coaptation point
Vena contracta neck just above the valve
Pulmonary vein entry into the left atrium
What to report: Mechanism: prolapse, flail, rheumatic restriction or tethering, with the scallop involved
Effective orifice, regurgitant volume and fraction with vena contracta width
Chamber sizes, ejection fraction and pulmonary pressure
Suitability clues for repair: leaflet length, calcification, annulus size and jet direction
Red flags needing urgent referral: Acute severe regurgitation with pulmonary oedema after infarction or endocarditis, needs emergency surgical review
Severe regurgitation with ejection fraction 60 percent or below or end systolic diameter 40 mm or more, needs prompt surgical review
Flail leaflet with a highly mobile segment, needs urgent review for repair timing
Pitfalls: Eccentric wall hugging jets read small on colour, so trust PISA and vein flow over jet area.
Late systolic prolapse gives a small PISA radius with a loud murmur, so time the measurement to the jet.
Blood pressure changes the grade within minutes, so record pressure and repeat when controlled.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the apical four chamber view and map the jet origin and direction with colour.
Zoom on the vena contracta and measure its narrowest width in millimetres.
Record continuous wave Doppler through the jet for density and peak velocity.
Measure the proximal flow convergence radius at an aliasing velocity of 30 to 40 cm per s for PISA quantitation.
Record pulmonary vein flow and left heart volumes for the supportive severe signs.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Grading by colour jet area which grows with gain and pressure. Fix: Grade by vena contracta, PISA radius and vein flow, not by how far the colour spreads into the atrium.
Measuring PISA with a high aliasing velocity that shrinks the shell. Fix: Lower the aliasing baseline to 30 to 40 cm per s and measure the first clear hemisphere in mid systole.
Calling severe disease from one pulmonary vein alone. Fix: Sample all four veins if possible. One reversed vein can reflect local compression, two confirm severe disease.

remember.en: Use chamber sizes and ejection fraction to time surgical referral.

q.en: Which effective orifice marks severe mitral regurgitation?

why.en: Severe is 0.40 sq cm or more with regurgitant volume 60 ml or more.

q.en: Which supportive sign confirms severe disease?

o.en: A soft ejection murmur at the base
A small central jet under 1 cm

why.en: Systolic reversal in the pulmonary vein is a specific severe sign alongside a dense triangular envelope.

q.en: An eccentric wall hugging jet looks small on colour. What settles the grade?

o.en: Vena contracta plus PISA radius plus vein flow

why.en: Wall hugging jets lose colour area, so vena contracta, PISA and vein flow give the true grade.

q.en: Severe regurgitation is found with ejection fraction 55 percent and no symptoms. What next?

why.en: Ejection fraction 60 percent or below with severe primary disease is a surgical trigger even without symptoms.
